question.text: Under SEBI AIF Regulations, what is the MINIMUM investment that a NON-employee, NON-accredited investor must commit to a Cat II AIF scheme?

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Regulations mandate a minimum investment of INR 1 crore per investor per scheme for ordinary (non-employee, non-accredited) investors. Employees and directors of the manager have a separate INR 25 lakh concession. Accredited Investors are governed under a separate AI framework that offers flexibility on the minimum investment amount; the AI minimum is NOT a fixed INR 25 lakh. The Trap: INR 25 lakh is the employee/director concession, not the ordinary LP floor and not a fixed AI minimum. INR 50 lakh and INR 5 crore are not the ordinary LP floor. Note: The workbook supports the INR 1 crore ordinary-investor minimum, the separate employee/director INR 25 lakh concession, and the distinct AI framework flexibility. The AI = INR 25 lakh claim has been removed.
